Documentation

  • Help Centre safeguarding guides match the vetting-based rules (26 October): ten admin, broker and member articles now say that new members are asked only the vulnerable-adult question; that coordinators and members with recorded vetting can contact a vulnerable member, both ways, and only coordinators until vetting is recorded; that groups keep working; and how Offer to new members closes an option. All eleven languages; Irish hand-written.
  • ASP.NET audit independently verified (25 October): a second reviewer re-traced every Codex finding in source. None was refuted; corrections are recorded, for example the legal-documents service already exists behind the wrong route, and the 33 route collisions share one root cause in the alias convention. The pass also found 16 further gaps, including no first-community or first-admin bootstrap for a new install, admin approval that does not allow sign-in, email verification that cannot complete, no starting balance, no exchange notifications, React group creation and image posts rejected, module switches with no effect, and an ASP.NET RSVP action that trusts a body user_id (not deployed). It also records that web-uk's insurance upload conflicts with live Laravel. Repaired run-together numbers and the 52/53 package mismatch in the Codex-written pages, and pointed to the detailed method text that pass removed. aspnet-backend/docs/CURRENT_ASPNET_CONTRACT_STATUS.md, ROADMAP.md. Development remains paused.
  • Audit documentation CI follow-up: corrected Markdown spacing in the maintained architecture, monorepo, dual-backend and documentation-index pages; no application behavior changed.
  • Dual-backend restart scope (25 October): clarified independent new installations with both web frontends unchanged; prepared an owned implementation/verification breakdown, effort scenarios, first-stage checklist and acceptance requirements. Existing-community data migration is excluded; delivery remains paused.
  • ASP.NET deeper readiness review (25 October): expanded workflow/lifecycle review, reproduced routing ambiguity, distinguished migration source counts from EF discovery, and refreshed restart sequence, handoff, coverage and acceptance guidance. Implementation remains paused.
  • ASP.NET readiness audit (25 October): reviewed current backend code against Laravel and both unchanged web frontends; recorded confirmed contract and persistence gaps, build/selected-test evidence, and verification limits. Reconciled maintained readiness and handoff guidance. Development remains paused; no compatibility certification or deployment is claimed.

Added

  • Accessible site catches up with the website — every member-facing gap from the 26 Oct React/accessible drift audit that does not need a card-payment or sign-in decision (owner: "address everything on the list"). New on web-uk, each as plain GOV.UK pages that work without JavaScript, gated exactly as React gates them, wording in all eleven languages: Help Centre — the 208 member guides plus the broker and admin guides at /help/{audience}/{section}/{article}, generated from React's own guide registries and help_* catalogues by web-uk/scripts/build-help-guides.js (build:help / check:help; a test fails when the copy is stale, and .github/ci-paths.yml now wakes the Web UK jobs when React's guides change), with the community FAQ kept on /help. Events — organisers assign event staff and create, change, pause and archive ticket types; "Create event" is hidden, and the form explained, where the community restricts who may create. Groups — filter the directory by group type with a type label on each card; redeem a group invitation link at /groups/invite/{token} (a signed-out visitor signs in and comes back — auth.js accepts only that exact return shape, lib/login-return.js), and organisers now see the link they minted. Comments and likes on events and volunteering opportunities. Volunteering — organisation safeguarding reports show an open/total count, what each status means, the confidentiality and "never contact the reporter" guidance, and no update form on a closed report; donations name the organisation and campaign, separate live/coming/past campaigns, offer cash and a payment reference, drop a donor total that counted people twice, and gain a receipt page; My hours pages through every entry and lists the shifts a member holds. Marketplace — browse borrow-and-lend items, follow and appeal reports, manage shipping options, add/replace/remove listing photos (lib/api.js now sends images[], so several photos are no longer reduced to the last one), and paging on every capped list, including the accepted-offer purchase that failed for a buyer with more than 50 sent offers. Partner communities — a profile now says up front when that community's safeguarding policy will refuse contact, and offers no form the server would refuse; the matches pages explain when vetting checks are unavailable. Clubs — invitations, a member's dues (amount and status; paying by card is not offered because the dues API is PaymentIntent-only), and the organiser's dues overview, reminders, waivers, fee settings, yearly generation and CSV member import. Also: regional points (balance, history, sending), the municipality calendar, a member's ad campaigns, the emailed supported-decision confirmation page, community pages in the footer menu (menu_pages), the community's own date and number format (settings.region), podcast studio guide and copyable share links, and Beta labels on Courses and Podcasts. Route matrix 854 -> 906; API ledger 776 -> 816 contracts, every helper with a direct contract assertion. Most journeys were walked on the disposable e2e environment; the rest are covered by tests, as recorded per item in the audit report. Tests: about 30 new web-uk/tests/* files; full web-uk suite 4,235 passing.

  • Accessible site — members can block a member of a partner community (F-284 parity, 26 Oct 2026). The website gained this on 29 Sep; the accessible site had no control, so a member there could not stop a partner-community member's messages, connection requests or credit transfers. A partner member's profile (/federation/members/{id}) now offers Block this member, and once blocked says so, offers Unblock member and offers no contact. It uses the existing member block endpoint and the profile's existing translated wording (no new strings). Only members of internal partner communities can be blocked: an external partner's member id belongs to another installation, so it is never offered and a forged form is refused before the API. New routes POST /federation/members/{id}/block and /unblock. Walked end to end on the disposable e2e environment (block stored, the partner's federated message then refused with BLOCKED, unblock restores contact). Tests: web-uk/tests/federation-partner-block.test.js (9).

  • Safeguarding — "I consider myself a vulnerable adult" switches on the community's vetting system (owner decisions, 25 Oct 2026, after the Timebanking UK chief executive confirmed that dealing with vulnerable adults requires vetting, in Ireland and the UK alike). It is the one safeguarding question new members are asked (with "none of these apply"). The option now carries requires_vetted_interaction with the jurisdiction's own check (garda_vetting, dbs_enhanced, pvg_scotland, access_ni, uk_safeguarding_clearance): coordinators of the member's community (any SafeguardingStaff role, new SafeguardingCoordinatorDirectory) and members whose vetting the community has recorded can contact the member; nobody else. It works both ways: the member can contact coordinators and vetted members only (code SAFEGUARDING_CONTACT_RESTRICTED with restricted_by_sender, wording safeguarding.errors.contact_via_coordinator*), instead of being able to send a message nobody was allowed to answer. Coordinators can always contact any member with a contact-limiting choice, including the older "coordinator arranges all contact" and "only vetted members" choices. Coordinator alerts name the right member when it is the protected member who tried to make contact (contact_attempt_via_body, coordination_request_via_body, reason SAFEGUARDING_CONTACT_VIA_COORDINATOR). Migration 2026_10_25_210000_vulnerable_adults_use_vetting applies this to existing communities; where a member already holds the option it keeps its coordinator-only block as well, so nobody becomes reachable by more people without choosing that. A coordinator-approved-contacts design was built earlier the same day and withdrawn before release, because an approval could have let an unvetted member contact a vulnerable adult. Wording hand-written in Irish, machine-translated in the other nine languages and spot-checked. Tests: VulnerableMemberContactTest (8); 15 existing test files updated for the new methods.

  • Safeguarding questions say what they do, and a member cut off by "vetted members only" can get out of it in one step (owner, 25 Oct 2026). Production check that day: on TimeBank Ireland (tenant 2) five members held "I would prefer to only interact with members who have been appropriately vetted", the community had recorded Garda Vetting for no one, so SafeguardingInteractionPolicy refused every message, reply, credit transfer, exchange, review, mention and group-chat post to them from anyone; tenants 5 and 11 had one such member each. The option was worded as a preference and promised "coordinators will ensure you are only matched with vetted members"; nothing did that. New SafeguardingEffectsService turns an option's enforced triggers into plain sentences in the member's language (including the live count of members with vetting recorded, e.g. "No members have Garda vetting recorded here at the moment, so nobody can contact you while this is on"); they are returned as effects by GET /v2/onboarding/safeguarding-options, GET /v2/safeguarding/my-preferences and GET /v2/admin/safeguarding/options (which also gains holder_count), and shown under every option in the website wizard, its post-save summary, Settings → Safeguarding, the broker/admin options page, the accessible site and the phone app. New option coordinator_introductions ("I would like a coordinator to keep an eye on my exchanges and help introduce me to members": broker approval of exchanges, match review, coordinator told; members can still message) in every preset and added to existing communities by migration 2026_10_25_200000_overhaul_safeguarding_questions. New tenant_safeguarding_options.accepts_new_selections: a closed option is hidden from members who do not hold it and refused by the API for them, while it keeps protecting, and stays visible to, its holders (closing never touches a live protection, so the F-433 guard is unaffected); staff can switch it from the options page. New member endpoint POST /v2/safeguarding/switch-to-coordinator-introductions (selects the new option and revokes vetted-only in one audited step; 409 when not held), with a button in Settings carrying server-translated copy. Emails (App\Services\Safeguarding\SafeguardingChoicesEmail, new table safeguarding_member_emails): an automatic "Your safety choices" summary ten minutes after a member saves or changes their choices (SendSafeguardingChoicesSummary, unique per member; listing only protections that are on; not repeated when nothing changed; none for "none of these apply"), and a one-off apology/explanation to vetted-only holders. Both are sent per member in their own language; neither is scheduled for existing members — php artisan safeguarding:send-choice-summaries [--notice] [--tenant=] --dry-run sends them when an operator decides. safeguarding:check-policy-health now also alerts (own Sentry fingerprint safeguarding_vetted_contact_unreachable) when members require vetted contact in a community that has recorded no vetting — tenant 2's state, which the check passed until now. Wording in all eleven languages; Irish hand-written. Tests: SafeguardingQuestionsOverhaulTest (9), SafeguardingChoicesEmailTest (8), SafeguardingPolicyHealthCheckTest (+1, one renamed), SafeguardingStep.test.tsx, SafeguardingTab.test.tsx (+3).

  • The offers & requests round-up email is back (owner, 25 Oct 2026). The original weekly email of new offers and requests was lost in the Laravel move: src/Services/DigestService.php was deleted on 20 Mar 2026 (df9906ee7), its Laravel replacement was an empty stub (deleted 21 Mar, aa27af479), and the design, views/emails/weekly_digest.php, went on 11 May as an "orphan email" (2d7ce86d8); nothing has sent it since. New App\Services\ListingsDigestService + ListingsDigest\ListingsDigestEmail (a new owner-approved design: hero with counts, a spotlight listing, Offers and "Could you help?" card sections, up to three upcoming public events, a post-an-offer prompt; brand colour from the community, darkened until white text reads at 4.5:1; stacked cards on phones, dark-mode aware, right-to-left for Arabic). Automatic: a daily 10:00 cron (listings-digest) emails each member whose own interval has passed — monthly by default, weekly selectable; a community admin sets the community default (listings_digest.default_frequency: monthly, weekly or off) and each member can choose their own (notification_preferences.listings_digest_frequency, email_listings_digest). A member is only ever sent listings they have not been sent before (new table listings_digest_sends), never their own, nothing from anyone they blocked or who blocked them, and no email when nothing is new; listings follow ListingService::applyPublicVisibility() plus not expired and an active poster; events are published, scheduled, not in a group. The poster is shown by first name only (or organisation name). On demand: Admin → Listings → Offers & requests email (/admin/listings-digest) shows a live preview, the default frequency and the number of members it would reach, and Send now emails every current offer and request to everyone who has not turned it off, after a confirmation; it runs on the emails queue in batches of 40 (App\Jobs\SendListingsDigestNow, not retried) and is audit-logged. Newsletters: a new {{recent_listings}} merge tag drops the newest offers and requests into any newsletter as the same cards (the old newsletter editor's "Listings" button, also lost in March). Endpoints: GET/PUT /v2/users/me/listings-digest, GET/PUT /v2/admin/listings-digest, GET /v2/admin/listings-digest/preview, POST /v2/admin/listings-digest/send. The member setting is in Settings → Notifications on the website and the accessible site; the email's one-click unsubscribe (category listings_digest) turns off only this email. Mail category listings_digest uses the newsletter sender and stream. "Post an offer" / "Ask for help" open the listing form with the type chosen (/listings/create?type=request). Wording hand-translated in all eleven languages (emails_listings.listings_digest.*, settings.listings_digest.*, admin_newsletters.listings_digest.*, govuk_alpha.profile_settings.notifications.round_up_*). Tests: ListingsDigestServiceTest (13), ListingsDigestControllerTest (7), ListingsDigestAdmin.test.tsx, ListingsDigestSetting.test.tsx, web-uk/tests/shared-accessible-shell.test.js.

  • Accessible site — the podcast studio and episode page now do what the website's do (owner, 25 Oct 2026; the remaining gaps from the same day's podcast audit). Studio (/podcasts/studio/{id}): one label per show and episode naming why listeners cannot hear it yet (draft, archived, awaiting review, not approved, scheduled for a time in UTC, audio still being checked, audio could not be used) or "Published"; moderator feedback shown under the show and each episode; Publish offered only when the API will accept it (a draft or archived episode whose audio is ready — it was offered for every non-published episode, so an episode still being virus-checked failed with "could not be published"); Archive for a show and for an episode, each behind a confirmation page, and publishing an archived one brings it back; deleting a whole show now goes through a confirmation page as one episode already did (it was one button press); subscriber count, and when listen analytics are on, listens, different listeners, the share listened to the end and the most listened-to episodes for the last 30 days (GET /v2/podcasts/{id}/stats); a podcast feed check page (GET /v2/podcasts/{id}/validate-feed) listing in plain words what must and should be fixed before podcast apps can read the feed. Every refusal now also shows the API's own reason, in the member's language (rememberApiReason(), kept for one page view) — they all collapsed into one generic message. Chapters are typed as plain lines ("0:00 Introduction", "1:02:30 Questions"), as on the website, instead of raw JSON (JSON is still accepted, for a chapter with a link), with their own error message. Scheduled times say they are UTC and are sent with the zone (…:00Z), so the API cannot read them in its own default zone. Episode page: Like this episode / Remove your like with a count, when the community has likes on (POST /v2/podcasts/episodes/{id}/reaction, sending the state wanted, not a toggle); Report this episode with a reason and details (…/report); the chapter list; and Download the transcript as a text file (/podcasts/{show}/episodes/{id}/transcript.txt, from this site because the API's distribution route serves public episodes only). Listening is not counted from this site: that needs the page's player script, which the accessible site does not have. 10 new routes, 4 new API contracts; wording hand-translated in all eleven languages (govuk_alpha.podcasts.*, govuk_alpha_commerce.podcast_studio.*; the chapter, chapter-error and schedule hints reworded). Tests: web-uk/tests/podcast-studio-gaps.test.js (17), podcast-episode-multipart-clears.test.js.

  • TimeBank Ireland's accessible site is live at accessible.hour-timebank.ie, and it is monitored (owner, 24 Oct 2026; tenant 2's accessible_domain). No new vhost was needed: hour-timebank.ie is a Plesk domain alias of project-nexus.ie, so the accessible.project-nexus.ie subdomain already answered as accessible.hour-timebank.ie and proxied it to web-uk. It returned Cloudflare 526 only because that vhost carried Lets Encrypt accessible.project-nexus.ie, which names one host. Let's Encrypt could not add the new name (the HTTP challenge is redirected to HTTPS, which is the part that was failing), so the vhost now uses cloudflare-origin-nexus-20260506 — the certificate app.project-nexus.ie already serves app.hour-timebank.ie with; it covers *.project-nexus.ie and *.hour-timebank.ie and runs to 2041. The Let's Encrypt certificate stays in the repository (valid to 3 Dec 2026) as the rollback. Verified live: /version on both hosts returns nexus-webuk, the new host serves TimeBank Ireland slug-less (no community chooser, /listings 200), the shared host still shows the chooser and /hour-timebank/accessible pages, both redirect HTTP to HTTPS. 🔴 The certificate binding lives only on the server. Both URLs (root, and /version expecting nexus-webuk) are added to scripts/uptime-targets.json, and the two deploy warnings that list the accessible hostnames name it.

  • Phone app and accessible site — profile stat cards open your own records, with My Listings / My Groups / My Events (owner, 24 Oct 2026; follows the website change below). Phone app (mobile/): on your own profile StatCard becomes a pressable (role button, label + hint) — Hours Given / Hours Received / Total hours → Wallet, Active Listings → new (modals)/my-listings (GET /v2/listings/mine, the website's five status groups with counts, paging, empty/error states; a "My listings" button on the Listings tab), Groups → groups with a new "My Groups" filter (user_id=<me>, ?scope=joined), Events → Events tab with a new "My Events" toggle (scope=mine, ?scope=mine). Gated by the same module/feature checks; plain on others' and federated profiles. Deep links /listings/mine, /groups?scope=joined, /events?scope=mine resolve natively; parity-map.json marks listings/mine native. 7 app locales. Tests: member-profile (+5), my-listings (7), groups (+3), events (+2), exchanges (+1), native-intent (+1); deepLinkParams resolver now follows @/app/ re-exports. Accessible site (web-uk/): own-profile activity figures link (inside the <dt>, visually hidden destination suffix) to /wallet, new /listings/mine (GET /v2/listings/mine, status tabs with counts, type filter, load more, sign-in required), /groups?filter=joined (existing) and /events?scope=mine (new; heading/intro change, scope kept through filters and paging, signed-out visitors sent to sign in); Groups and Events figures added when those features are on. "My listings", "My groups", "My events" buttons on the three index pages. 25 new govuk_alpha.own_records.* strings hand-translated in all eleven languages; route matrix and API ledger regenerated. Tests: own-records-links.test.js (10), api.test.js.

  • Profile stat cards are clickable, and Events has a "My Events" view (owner, 24 Oct 2026). On your own profile the five cards now open the matching page: Hours Given and Hours Received → /wallet, Active Listings → /listings/mine, Groups → /groups?scope=joined (the existing "My Groups" filter), Events → /events?scope=mine. On someone else's profile the cards stay plain, since those pages show your own records. The link stretches over the whole card so the <dl> keeps valid dt/dd markup. New GET /v2/events?scope=mine (EventService::whereMine()) lists only events you organise or have RSVP'd "going" to; the recurring-series collapse applies the same rule to sibling occurrences, so the occurrence you are going to is not hidden behind one you are not. A guest asking for it gets nothing. The Events page gets a "My Events" toggle (hero and phone row, aria-pressed, kept in the URL); arriving with ?scope=mine starts on "All events" so past attended events match the profile count. My Listings and My Groups already existed and are unchanged. New events.my_events.* keys, hand-translated in all eleven languages. Tests: EventDiscoveryContractTest (2 new), ProfilePage.test.tsx (2 new).

  • Admin — the SEO page no longer warns that Google verification is missing on sites verified another way. /admin/seo showed "Google Search Console Verification — Not configured — recommended for search insights" as a warning whenever its verification box was empty, although Google offers several methods and most communities use a DNS TXT record (the only one for a Domain property; hour-timebank.ie was verified that way through Cloudflare), so a correctly verified site looked faulty. New GET /v2/admin/config/seo-verification-dns (admin; App\Services\SearchVerificationDns) looks up the community's own domain and its parent domains for a google-site-verification= TXT record (cached 6 h when found, 10 min when not; a resolver failure reads as not found and is logged). The health check now passes with "A Google verification record was found in the DNS settings for {domain}" when one exists, and otherwise shows a neutral note (not counted in the score) saying it can be ignored if the site was verified another way and that nothing is broken; a community on a shared address (<app host>/<slug>), whose DNS is the platform's, is not looked up and is pointed at the box instead. The verification card says both boxes are optional and that Bing can copy verification from Google Search Console. Bing's DNS method (a CNAME named after the account's own code) cannot be looked up and is not checked. A record shows someone verified the domain, not which Google account or that it is still current; the wording says only what was found. The old warning string leaves all eleven languages; the new wording is hand-translated in all eleven. Tests: SeoVerificationDnsTest (7), SeoOverview.test.tsx (6 new).

  • "Site for search engines" — a community can make its accessible site the one search engines index (seo_primary_site on /admin/seo: standard, the default, or accessible; 2026-10-23). For communities such as councils that use only the accessible site. With accessible: the main site's sitemap answers 404 (SitemapService::notListedReason() → accessible_primary) and the accessible site publishes its own; llms.txt describes the community with its accessible addresses (/timebanking-guide → /guide, coupons left out); on the main site every page with an accessible equivalent names it as canonical and og:url, and a page with none gets noindex, follow and no canonical (src/components/seo/primarySite.ts, accessibleFrontendEquivalentFor()); breadcrumb data is not emitted, and SeoHead's Organization and WebSite url/@id and the x-default hreflang use the accessible site. On the accessible site (web-uk) every public page becomes self-canonical in this mode, and there is now a sitemap in both modes (src/lib/accessible-sitemap.js: /sitemap.xml on a community's accessible domain, /{slug}/accessible/sitemap.xml on the shared host). In standard mode it lists only the pages that are canonical to themselves (changelog releases, single legal versions); in accessible mode every public signed-out page, blog posts and upcoming public events included, with the module and feature gates applied. It answers 404 for hidden communities or when the automatic sitemap is off, 503 uncached when the API fails, and robots.txt names it when published. seo:probe checks the canonicals point at the accessible site and that its sitemap has addresses. standard output is unchanged. The value is validated (422 api.seo_primary_site_invalid, 11 locales) and published in the tenant bootstrap. Tests: SeoFieldParityTest, SitemapControllerTest, LlmsControllerTest, SeoProbeTest, PageMeta.test.tsx, SeoHead.test.tsx, SeoOverview.test.tsx, web-uk/tests/seo-accessible-primary-sitemap.test.js.

  • Help Centre guides in every community's sitemap (owner, 23 Oct 2026: every community indexes its own). SitemapService::getHelpGuideUrls() lists /help/brokers, /help/admins and every section and article the community actually has, with the Help Centre's own gates (registry.ts isGateOpen: feature and module gates need the switch on, setting gates count as open as for a signed-out visitor); /help/members is the same page as /help and is not listed. Until now this returned [], so every guide reached crawlers as the bare shell with noindex. The guide list is the React registry, copied to resources/help/*.registry.json because the API image ships no react-frontend/; HelpRegistryCopyTest fails if the copy drifts. /help/** gets a 30-day snapshot TTL. About 350 guide pages per community: the first render after deploy is a one-time several-hour job, after which only changed guides re-render. Tests: SitemapServiceTest (guides listed and gated; older substring checks ignore help addresses), HelpRegistryCopyTest.

  • seo:probe, a nightly check of what search engines receive (06:15, runInBackground, guarded by PagerCommandsRunInBackgroundTest). For each community it fetches / and /about as Googlebot (one <title>, canonical = own address, noindex only when the community is hidden), its sitemap (200 with addresses, or 404 when hidden or switched off), its host's robots.txt (names this host's sitemap) and llms.txt (404 when hidden). Problems are logged, sent to Sentry once (fingerprint seo_probe) and to the SLO Slack webhook, and the command exits non-zero, as slo:check does. Until now nothing on a schedule looked at the live site as a crawler. Tests: tests/Laravel/Feature/Console/SeoProbeTest.php.

  • Phone app — "Trust this device" at the two-factor step. The app had no such option, so every sign-in on a phone asked for the authenticator code. When the community allows it, the code screen now offers "Trust this device for N days"; the token the server issues (trusted_device_token, already returned to native clients) is kept in secure storage, one per account (community + email), and sent as X-Trusted-Device at the next sign-in for that account. Signing out keeps it, as on the website. Wording in the app's seven languages. Ships to phones by over-the-air update after the server change is deployed (no native change). Tests: lib/trustedDevices.test.ts, lib/api/auth.test.ts (token stored and kept out of the session, never requested when not allowed, sent at sign-in), MfaSignIn.test.tsx (offered with the day limit, off unless ticked, hidden when not allowed).

  • CI — no migration may overwrite or remove content a community wrote (BLOCKING). Deploys run pending migrations automatically, so a migration that changes community-written content replaces what the community chose on every server that has not run it yet; migrations/2026_05_13_normalize_hour_timebank_branding.sql did exactly that to hour-timebank's name, meta title, title suffix and footer. scripts/check-tenant-content-writes.mjs (npm run check:tenant-content-writes, in the Migration Safety Gate, which runs on every push, and in preflight.mjs) fails when a file in database/migrations/ or migrations/ overwrites or deletes: the tenants fields a community edits (SEO tab, General, Contact, Social: meta title and description, hub heading and intro, sharing image, robots, organisation type, name, tagline, description, contact details, social links); its branding in tenants.configuration (footer text, logos, favicon, colour); the landing_page.config, seo_* and footer_text settings; or existing rows of the content tables (custom pages and their blocks and versions, menus and menu items, legal documents and versions, help articles and FAQs, knowledge base, blog, newsletter templates). Schema changes, NEW rows and insert-if-missing defaults are allowed. A migration that genuinely must do it carries tenant-content-overwrite: approved — <who, why>. Eleven older files that did this (all already applied; applied migrations never re-run) are recorded in .github/tenant-content-writes-baseline.json, which only shrinks. Pinned both ways by scripts/test/test-tenant-content-writes.sh (eight overwrites refused; six schema, new-row, default, approved and operational writes allowed).

  • Admin — the social sharing image can be uploaded, and the field explains itself. On /admin/seo ("Social sharing image") and the super-admin tenant form's SEO tab, the bare "OG Image URL" box is replaced by SharingImageField: a plain explanation (the picture shown when a link to the community is shared on Facebook, WhatsApp, LinkedIn, X and most messaging apps; pages without their own picture use it), the size to use (1200 × 630 px, JPG or PNG, under 1 MB, nothing important near the edges), an Upload image button that sends the file to the tenant image library (POST /v2/upload, admin-only, 10 MB cap) and fills the address in, a Replace / Remove pair, the address box for pasting an image that is already online, a preview that says when the address shows no image, and a reminder that the page's Save button keeps it. Wording hand-translated in all eleven languages. Tests: SharingImageField.test.tsx (explanation, upload fills the address, upload failure leaves it alone, remove, paste).

  • Accessible site — the people who run a shift can check a volunteer in and out. /volunteering/checkin/{code}, the same address as the website's check-in page, asks first (opening it changes nothing), then Confirm they have arrived checks the volunteer in (POST /v2/volunteering/checkin/verify/{code}) and names them, and Check them out checks them out. The API's own refusals (checking yourself in, checking out before the shift starts) are shown in its words. The volunteer's QR code still opens the website's page; this one serves a coordinator who uses the accessible site. New wording hand-translated in all eleven languages.

  • Accessible site — community projects are listed again, and members can propose and support them. The Community projects tab (/volunteering?tab=community_projects) had always said there were no projects: it read the API's reply as a list when it is { items, cursor, has_more }. It now shows the community's approved, active and completed projects with who proposed them, where, when and how many volunteers are needed, and each has Support this project or Remove your support. Propose a project opens /volunteering/community-projects/propose (title, description, and optional category, place, number of volunteers and start date); a proposal returns to the tab saying it will appear once an administrator approves it. New wording hand-translated in all eleven languages.

  • Accessible site — who applied to one opportunity. The people who run an opportunity now have Review applications on its page, opening /volunteering/opportunities/{id}/applications: that opportunity's applicants (GET /v2/volunteering/opportunities/{id}/applications), waiting for a decision by default, with Approved / Declined / All tabs and load more. Each waiting application has the same approve-or-decline form, with an optional note, as the organisation review list, and the organiser comes back to the same tab with the outcome; a decided one shows its status and note. Until now the accessible site had only the organisation-wide list. Not built: the website's tick-several-and-approve-all and its search of the loaded names.
